organization: Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal (OSFM)
title: Fire Equipment Distributor License Application (Revised 01/16/2025)
claim: Illinois fire equipment distributor license classes and fees (3-year term): Class A extinguishers $900; Class B pre-engineered systems $1,500; Class C engineered systems $2,100. Requires $1,000,000 liability insurance, workers' comp, USDOT PHMSA RIN (or arrangement with a RIN holder) for hydrotesting/visual inspection of DOT cylinders, and a licensed employee in the matching class.
excerpt: Class A: Will service, recharge, hydro-test, install, maintain, or inspect all types of fire extinguishers. (Fee: $900.00)
limitations: Fees shown on application form; invoiced after approval. Form revision 01/16/2025 (PDF modified 2025-06-23).

organization: Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal (OSFM)
title: Fire Equipment Distributor Employee License Application (Revised 01/16/2025)
claim: Fire equipment employee license classes (Class 1 extinguishers, 2I industrial pre-engineered, 2K kitchen pre-engineered, 3 engineered), $300 per class, valid 3 years; must be 18+; requires ICC or NAFED certification (Class 1/2I/2K) or NAFED engineered / NICET III special hazards (Class 3); must be employed by a licensed distributor.
excerpt: Class 1: ICC or NAFED certification in Portable Fire Extinguishers... Must be 18 years of age or older.
limitations: Does not state exam pass rates or study time; certification costs (ICC/NAFED) not on form.

organization: Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal (OSFM)
title: Fire Equipment Distributors - Update P.A. 102-0715 (fact sheet)
claim: Fire Equipment Distributor and Employee Regulation Act of 2011 covers servicing of portable extinguishers and pre-engineered/engineered suppression systems; P.A. 102-0715 requires $1M liability insurance, workers comp, a licensed employee per license type, separate license per location (no branch licenses), and 3 years of service records.
excerpt: Distributors are no longer able to apply for a branch office license. Each fire equipment distributor must apply for its own distributor license for each location
limitations: Fact sheet summary, not the statute text; Justia compilation notes the Act has a scheduled repeal (sunset) date of 1 Jan 2028 - renewal status unverified.

organization: U.S. Census Bureau, County Business Patterns
title: County Business Patterns 2023, state-level file (cbp23st.txt), Illinois (fipstate 17)
claim: Illinois 2023 establishments (employees; annual payroll): 561710 pest control 395 est (3,444 emp; $188.7M); 561720 janitorial 2,520 (50,936; $1.65B); 561730 landscaping 5,034 (23,331); 561740 carpet/upholstery 296; 561790 other services to buildings 463 (3,441; $143.6M); 238220 plumbing/HVAC 4,070 (41,112); 238290 other building equipment contractors (incl. elevator) 344 (5,900; $646.8M); 238160 roofing 1,026; 561621 security systems services 187 (4,144); 561612 guard services 356 (34,528); 562991 septic & related 81 (559); 541350 building inspection 234; 811310 commercial machinery repair 873; 423850 service establishment equipment wholesale 263. Majority of establishments in each have <5 employees (e.g., 561710: 219 of 395; 561790: 338 of 463).

organization: Environmental Resources Training Center, SIU Edwardsville
title: Cross-Connection Control Device Inspector (CCCDI) course page
claim: Illinois EPA CCCDI certification requires a four-day (24-hour) training course, listed at $650 per course in 2026 sessions (Joliet, Murphysboro, Rockford, Champaign); annual renewal.
excerpt: Current IEPA Cross-Connection Control Device Inspector certification requires a four-day training course.
limitations: Page does not itself state the plumbing-license prerequisite; renewal fee not shown.

title: Cross Connection Control program page
claim: Facilities possessing backflow prevention devices must have them inspected and tested at installation and at least annually thereafter; Illinois EPA runs the CCCDI approval program via ERTC/SIUE.
excerpt: Industries or facilities installing or possessing backflow prevention devices must have those devices inspected and tested at the time of installation and at least annually thereafter.
limitations: No fee, headcount, or plumbing-license detail on the page; no update date.

organization: Illinois Administrative Code (via Justia Regulations; text seen in search snippet)
title: 35 Ill. Adm. Code 653.802 - CCCDI approval qualifications
claim: Each applicant for CCCDI approval must meet the qualifications to inspect plumbing and plumbing systems under the Illinois Plumbing License Law (i.e., effectively an Illinois licensed plumber).
excerpt: Must meet the qualifications to inspect plumbing and plumbing systems as described in the Illinois Plumbing License Law.
limitations: Page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; language taken from search-result snippet of the rule; current amendment date unverified. Some municipal ordinances (e.g., Galesburg) also expressly require a licensed plumber.

organization: Illinois Administrative Code via Cornell LII
title: 77 Ill. Adm. Code 890.1130 - Protection of Potable Water (Illinois Plumbing Code)
claim: RPZ, RPDA, DCA and DCDA backflow assemblies must be tested and approved by a CCCDI before initial operation and at least annually thereafter; records kept on site.
excerpt: shall be tested and approved by a Cross-Connection Control Device Inspector (CCCDI) before initial operation
limitations: Amended effective 2014-04-24 per page; local water utilities layer their own reporting systems/fees.

organization: Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal (OSFM)
title: Fire Sprinkler Contractor Rules 2023 Fact Sheet (41 Ill. Adm. Code 109; P.A. 102-0612)
claim: Fire sprinkler inspectors must be employed and licensed through a licensed fire sprinkler contractor; minimum age 21; qualifications such as NICET III Inspection & Testing of Water-Based Systems, NFPA WBITM, ASSE 15010 or a DOL sprinkler-fitter apprenticeship; 2-year license with annual CE; unlicensed practice civil penalty up to $10,000; proposed fees $3,000 per contractor license and $500 per inspector license.
excerpt: A fire sprinkler inspector must be employed and licensed through the fire sprinkler contractor.
limitations: Fact sheet describes PROPOSED rules (May 2023); adopted final fee amounts not verified (adopted rule notice confirms fees were set/increased). Contractor-level 'designated certified person' qualification not confirmed from primary text.

organization: Illinois Administrative Code via Cornell LII
title: 41 Ill. Adm. Code 100.7 - Adoption of NFPA 101 Life Safety Code
claim: Illinois OSFM adopts NFPA 101 Life Safety Code (2015) in its entirety with OSFM modifications (effective 1/1/2020); references NFPA 80 (2013) for fire doors. NFPA 10/25/72/96 are not named in this section (they apply via NFPA 101 references and local codes).
excerpt: NFPA 101, Life Safety Code (2015) (adopted in its entirety, subject to the OSFM modifications in subsection (c)).
limitations: Chain of reference from NFPA 101 (2015) Chapter 9 to NFPA 10/25/72/96 not verified from primary text in this pass; Chicago enforces its own municipal fire/building codes.

title: Structural Pest Control program page
claim: A structural pest control business license requires employing at least one certified technician plus proof of insurance; annual renewal by Dec 1; technicians pass General Standards exam (+ subcategory exams for restricted-use), 70% passing, 3-year certification. Illinois has about 750 licensed structural pest control business locations and about 2,600 certified individuals.
excerpt: To obtain a LICENSE, a business must first employ at least one person who is a CERTIFIED TECHNICIAN.
limitations: Counts are approximate and undated on page.

title: Commercial Structural Pest Control Business License Application (2022)
claim: Business location license application fee $250; must list certified technician(s); IDPH certificate of insurance per Section 9 of the Act; pesticide storage well-distance disclosures.
excerpt: must be submitted with the certificate of insurance form and a $250 fee.
limitations: Insurance minimum amounts are in the Act Section 9 (not fetched).

title: Structural Pest Control Certification Application (General-Use)
claim: Technician certification exam application fee $75; asks HS/GED; no stated work-experience prerequisite on form; reciprocity for IN, IA, WI, MO certifications.
excerpt: This application for examination must be submitted to the above address with the $75 fee.
limitations: Form dated 2017; fee may have changed; restricted-use form not reviewed.
